core_obligations: Prove the intersection equals the product by showing the reverse inclusion with a partition-of-unity argument, which also gives injectivity of the natural map (proof lines 2846-2870).
Prove surjectivity of the natural map by constructing elements with prescribed residues, and deduce assertion (2) from the comaximality of distinct maximal ideals (proof lines 2870-2881).
proof_roadmap: Compare intersection and product and get injectivity (proof lines 2846-2870).
Construct the residues for surjectivity and read off (2) (proof lines 2870-2882).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives the Chinese remainder theorem: for pairwise comaximal ideals the intersection equals the product and the quotient by the product splits as a product of the quotients, with the case of pairwise distinct maximal ideals as a corollary (statement lines 2832-2844). The proof does not quote the theorem: it proves the intersection identity by a partition-of-unity argument, gets injectivity from it, and constructs explicit elements with prescribed residues for surjectivity (proof lines 2846-2882). The explicit construction of the residues is the step that carries surjectivity. H2.
